We are all pretending to have the best time of our lives, but it all feels like this massive, desperate performance to ignore how completely directionless and empty we all are.
sandhi_response: Feeling profoundly alone in a loud, celebrating crowd is a deeply painful experience, yet it shows how much your spirit craves real connection over a loud performance. It is completely okay to step away from the noise and rest in the quiet validity of what you are actually feeling right now.

user_input: I'm in my final semester, only a few weeks away from graduation, and everyone is talking about moving to Bangalore or Hyderabad and setting up their flats. But when I look at that future—renting a 1BHK, sitting in traffic, coding for some fintech giant—my chest just tightens up. It feels like I'm about to step off a cliff into a lifetime of grey, mundane routine that means absolutely nothing to me.
sandhi_response: It is terrifying to look ahead and see only a rigid, gray box waiting for you when your soul is longing for color and purpose. You do not have to accept that the future is predefined or empty; we can explore how to build a life that leaves room for your own quiet pockets of joy and meaning.

user_input: I cracked a 9.4 CGPA this semester, finished my DSA sheet, and my parents are already bragging about my upcoming placements to the relatives. But honestly? I sat on my terrace tonight and felt absolutely nothing. Just this hollow, empty pit. I’ve done everything I was supposed to do, but it feels like I'm just climbing a ladder that leans against a blank wall. What is even the point of all this grind if the prize at the end feels just as empty?
sandhi_response: It is incredibly disorienting to reach the milestones you worked so hard for, only to find that the achievement itself doesn't quiet the quiet ache inside you. Your feelings are not a failure of gratitude, but a gentle, albeit painful, signal from your soul that you are worth so much more than a collection of gold stars.

user_input: Every single day I open LinkedIn and see people from my batch posting about their 40 LPA packages and Google internships. I tried coding today but stared at the screen for three hours without writing a line of Python. It's like my brain has gone completely offline because it realized how utterly meaningless my little efforts are in this massive ocean. Even if I get that job, I'll just be another corporate cog spending 10 hours a day debugging code for someone else's profit—why do we pretend this is living?
sandhi_response: When you are constantly bombarded by the curated highlights of everyone else's race, it makes complete sense that your mind would want to shut down to protect itself from the noise. It is okay to step away from the screen and remind yourself that your worth cannot be measured by a job title or a corporate salary.

user_input: I wake up at 7 AM, rush to attendance-mandatory lectures, write lab records I don't care about, go back to my hostel, eat cold mess food, and sleep. I looked at my schedule for the next two years and literally started crying because it's just this identical loop over and over. I feel like a ghost inhabiting a student's body, just watching myself go through the motions without any real spark or purpose. Is this all adult life is going to be—just a series of boxes to check until we die?
sandhi_response: Living on autopilot can make you feel like a stranger in your own life, especially when the path ahead looks like a conveyor belt you never asked to board. Let's start very small tonight by honoring that exhaustion, rather than trying to fix it or figure out the next ten years right now.

user_input: I turned twenty last week and it hit me like a train. I've spent my entire youth studying for board exams, JEE, and now college GPA, and for what? I don't even know what I actually like or who I am when I'm not studying. I feel like I've traded my real, actual life for a piece of paper and a career path I don't even care about, and now I'm too deep into this engineering branch to change anything.
sandhi_response: It is incredibly heavy to feel like you have spent your youth meeting other people's expectations, leaving your own desires behind in the rush. Please know that turning twenty is not the end of your story, but the very place where you can begin to gently discover who you are outside of the classroom.

user_input: Everyone around me is preparing for placement season like it's a war they've been training for their whole lives, discussing packages, mock interviews, and resume building in the mess. I listen to them and I feel completely detached, like I'm speaking a different language. I don't want to compete, I don't want to climb the ladder, but I also don't know what else to do, so I just sit in my room staring at the ceiling feeling this immense, crushing weight of uselessness.
sandhi_response: Watching everyone run toward a finish line that you don't even want to cross can make you feel profoundly isolated and lost. It is completely natural to pause and question the race, and you deserve the space to figure out your own direction without feeling forced to run at their speed.
